core_findings: The model is an installed-base lifecycle system: systems are sold or leased, then procedure growth drives instruments/accessories and service revenue.

FY2025 revenue mix is approximately 59.8% instruments/accessories, 24.6% systems and 15.6% service; management-defined recurring revenue reached 85% in Q2/H1 2026 but includes economically different revenue types.
Usage-based operating leases deepen lifecycle alignment while remaining less contractually sticky than subscription revenue.
FY2025 gross margin was about 66.0% and operating margin about 29.3% while R&D remained about 13.0% of revenue.
Q2 2026 revenue grew 19%, da Vinci procedures 15% and Ion procedures 36%, demonstrating continued scale growth.
Economic quality is tempered by growing inventory, receivables and lease-fleet capital requirements plus material SBC.

canonical_verdict_fields.PRIMARY_MOAT: Installed-base ecosystem and procedure-linked lifecycle economics reinforced by service, workflow integration, training infrastructure, R&D scale, IP and clinical support.

core_findings: The strongest moat evidence is ecosystem depth around a large installed base, service/training infrastructure, procedure-linked consumables and sustained innovation, not hard surgeon skill lock-in.
Independent evidence that robotic skills can transfer across platforms directly limits a hard-switching-cost thesis.
Hugo, OTTAVA and Versius now have U.S. regulatory access, so contestability is rising even though current Intuitive scale remains substantially larger.
Da Vinci procedure growth of 15%, installed-base growth of 12%, utilization growth of 3% and Ion procedure growth of 36% support continued penetration and lifecycle growth.
da Vinci 5 mix, Ion adoption, international depth and indications provide multiple runway vectors without requiring a fabricated TAM denominator.
Hospital capital budgets, reimbursement economics, China quotas and credible U.S. entrants are real constraints on extrapolation.
Reconstructed FY2025 Standard ROIC is approximately 31.3% on an operating carrying-capital basis that retains goodwill and intangibles.
A one-year aggregate ROIIC diagnostic is approximately 40.8%, but investment lag, leasing capital and product-mix changes make it unsuitable as product-level ROIIC.
Return quality is clearly strong at group level; attribution to da Vinci 5, Ion, R&D cohorts or the Southern Europe acquisition is unavailable.
Three-year CFO/net-income conversion is about 103%, supporting accounting-to-cash coherence.
Conventional FCF rose to about $2.49bn in 2025, but maintenance versus growth capital is not supportably separated.
Lease-system inventory-to-PP&E transfers create timing complexity; subtracting the noncash transfer again from CFO would double count, so Owner Earnings remains UNKNOWN rather than fabricated.
R&D remained roughly 13% of revenue and liquidity stayed above $8.6bn at Q2 2026, supporting internally funded innovation and resilience.
2025 repurchases were about $2.30bn and H1 2026 repurchases about $1.44bn, but buyback value creation is not judged in Fundamentals because that requires valuation.
SBC is material and the March 2026 Southern Europe distribution acquisition is too recent for realized-return attribution.
David J. Rosa became CEO on July 1, 2025 while Gary Guthart moved to Executive Chair, providing continuity through the leadership transition.
Incentives explicitly include operating income, adoption, innovation, operational excellence and quality/regulatory objectives.
The new CEO's standalone outcome record remains short, limiting confidence in a long-duration stewardship conclusion.
Randomized and systematic-review evidence does not support universal robotic clinical or cost superiority; outcomes vary by procedure and robotic surgery is frequently more expensive.
Cross-platform skill transfer weakens a hard lock-in narrative, while new U.S. approvals show credible platform entry is feasible.
Titan Medical's failure shows entry remains capital- and commercialization-intensive, so regulatory entry alone does not imply successful scale.
Large cash and investment balances plus strong operating cash generation provide substantial financial resilience.

Key non-financial risks are credible robotic entrants, procedure-specific cost/clinical economics, product recalls, China policy/quotas, single/sole-source supply exposure, hospital budgets/reimbursement and cyber/software risks.

risks.early_indicator: competitor placements, procedure growth, hospital multi-platform adoption
risks.transmission_mechanism: Hugo, OTTAVA and Versius can weaken placement share, utilization, pricing and lifecycle revenue capture.

risks.early_indicator: procedure-specific RCT/meta-analysis outcomes and hospital cost studies
risks.transmission_mechanism: If clinical or workflow benefits do not justify system and procedure economics, adoption or utilization can slow.

risks.early_indicator: Class I/II recalls, adverse-event trends, regulatory actions
risks.transmission_mechanism: Quality failures can interrupt procedures, impair trust and raise remediation or liability costs.

risks.early_indicator: single-source disruptions, tariff exposure, component lead times
risks.transmission_mechanism: Component constraints can delay placements and instruments/accessories supply.

risks.early_indicator: quota/tender rules, local pricing limits, competitor approvals
risks.transmission_mechanism: Quota and pricing policy can constrain placements and procedure economics.

risks.early_indicator: inventory growth, lease-fleet PP&E growth, FCF conversion
risks.transmission_mechanism: A growing lease fleet and working capital can absorb cash ahead of utilization and revenue.
